header.title: Curse tablets from Britannia, in Latin (Epigraphic Database Heidelberg): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Latin curse tablets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:britannia-lat:lat, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.1027.10: 1027 and 1036 are names from lists, without the rest of their tablets. 1030.1.10: a word is lost before dea Sulis, probably 'him'; maximo letum, 'to the greatest death', is ungrammatical and its construction uncertain. caracella/caracalla is a hooded cloak. 1030.2.2-3: donec 'until' is split across the lines, its second half restored. 1033.5 repeats 'who have sworn' by error; it is not translated twice. 1036.1: the name carries an editorial letter-correction and its form is uncertain.
notes.7734.8: 7734.8-9 end a curse whose beginning lies outside the unit; destina(t), 'appoints', is unclear in sense. 8086: nisi 'until' is written twice; the petitioner moves from 'he' to 'me'; ipse may be the god or Cenacus. 8089: ⟦Mars Silvanus⟧ is erased on the tablet; ACA (2.4) is unexplained letters; 2.7 ends in a lost verb. 8092 is broken: er[it] 'will be' is partly restored and its construction unclear; fec[it] 'has committed' is completed by the restoration at the start of 8092.5; letters are lost after r in 8092.6. 8098: words of the SATOR-AREPO word square, whose overall sense is disputed.
notes.66.2.3: 66.2 ends a list of names: the tablet has VALAUNEICUS, corrected by the editor, and Belia() is an unexpanded abbreviation written with a superfluous a. 90.10: redemat and nessi are misspellings of redimat 'buy back' and nisi 'except'. 93.2: qui is taken as 'what' (for quod); the sentence continues beyond the unit.
notes.53281.1: 53281 ends a list of names. 53285.6: rogaverim (subjunctive) is rendered 'I would ask'; the genius is the guardian spirit of the god's power. 53285.13: concordiam habuerit, 'has my goodwill', may mean 'has made his peace with me'. 55268.2: the stolen object is lost except C[...]LAM, perhaps caracallam 'hooded cloak'.
notes.1045.4: 1045.4-5: dextrale (written DESTRALE), split with the line before, may be a bracelet or an axe. 1048: the start of 1048.3 is lost, and the tablet breaks off after 1048.5; ex{s}igatur has a superfluous s. 1051.1.5: mantutene is read as a mother's name, 'son of Matutina', which is uncertain. 1051.1.7-8: INDEPREG[.]STUM is unexplained and left as written. 1051.1.9: (r)eputes, 'charge to account', depends on a supplied letter. 1057: a fragment; A may be 'from' or an initial, and Nase[...] and Vroc[...] are incomplete names.
notes.96.4.2: 96.4 ends a list of names; Seni⟨i⟩la carries an editorial letter-correction and its form is uncertain. 1024.1: a word is lost after donavi, and argentiolos, 'little silver coins', is partly restored. 1024.6: carta picta perscripta, literally 'the painted sheet written out', is obscure; the three names are then listed again. 1027 begins another list of names.
notes.19330.4: 19330.4-5: exesuerit is unclear, perhaps 'has consumed' or 'has stripped'; dona may be 'gifts' or the command 'give'. 24366: fata is taken as 'words spoken'; SINIT (24366.7) is unexplained; amare 'to love' is split across 24366.7-9 among the edition's alternative spellings, so 24366.8 holds that word alone; the start of 24366.10 is lost. 25425: palleum is for pallium 'cloak', galliculae are Gallic shoes, and sanguinei is for sanguine. 25800.1.2: defic(t)us stands for defixus, 'bound by a curse'.
notes.69587.1: 69587 is a fragment; only Dad[...] survives. 69604.1.4: dimidiam partem, 'a half share', rendered 'half its value'. 69604.1.7: the editor reads non illis 'not to them' from the tablet's NOLLIS (perhaps nollis 'do not'), with the same sense; inter quibus nomen Seniciani is rendered literally. 69604.2.1: Rediviva, 'come back to life', is written apart on the other face; it may mark the curse as renewed, or be a woman's name.
notes.79549.4: 79549 is a broken fragment. 79550.3: pax{s}a ba(ln)earis, apparently a bathing garment, is a rare word; [pal]leum 'cloak' is partly restored. 79550.6: se retegens is taken as 'revealing himself'. 79550.8-9 are broken: [li]beri may be 'children' or 'free men', and deg and xe are remnants of lost words.
notes.1057.13: 1057.13-14 end a list of stolen goods; fascia may be a sash or a band; e carta s(upra) s(cripta) ratio(n)e, perhaps 'according to the sheet written above', is obscure. 1464.1.1-2: exc-on(f)ic[tu]s est, rendered 'is utterly accursed', is a rare and partly restored word. The tablet has PURE for puer 'boy'.
notes.48868.2: 48868 is broken; the capitals are unreadable remnants, and lamilla is probably a small metal plate. 49547.3: |(solidum) is a gold coin; Muconi is read as 'from Muco', though it could be the genitive of a name Muconius. 49547.8: Niske, vocative of a god Niskus, otherwise unidentified. 49547.11: fueris stands for fuerit; 49547.12: animus seems to stand for animum, 'the mind'.
notes.9.1: 9.1 is an alphabet written on a tablet. 12.1.1 Primurudem is unexplained. 12.2-3: anilum, liminibus and ob are read as anulum 'ring', luminibus 'eyes' and et 'and'; medius fuerit, 'has been a go-between', means an accomplice; configatur, 'be transfixed', is the language of binding curses.
notes.79429.1.1: Fragments: only the name Cunovinna and a dedication to Mars survive; the rest is lost.
notes.8942.6: Four separate texts. 8942: only the end survives; 'cias' is the tail of a lost verb, taken as [fa]cias, 'cause'; line 7 keeps only '-um'. 8951 (Biccus): 'm-ascet' is taken as mascel, 'male'; 'ne conscientiam de perferat' is obscure and 'gain awareness of it' is a guess. 12422: Metunus is a name I cannot identify, perhaps a garbled Neptunus; 'numene' is probably nomine, 'name' (possibly numine, 'divine power'). 12425: a list of names; the '#' separates the edition's expanded, corrected and as-written forms of each. Single restored letters inside otherwise legible words are not bracketed in the English.
notes.12428.1: '[...]eocorotis' is the end of a name that cannot be identified. laena (restored), pallium and sagum are three kinds of cloak; paxsa is unexplained (perhaps baxea, a sandal). rostrum is literally 'beak' or 'snout', apparently for 'mouth'. caballarem, 'of a horse', is taken as a horse-cloth; uncertain. Single restored letters inside otherwise legible words are not bracketed.
notes.15967.11: 15967 is the end of a theft curse: 'Digni' (genitive) completes the victim's name begun before this unit. pariat is taken as 'pay (in full)'; esto, 'let it be', is awkward and may go with decima pars. 18602 is a separate tablet whose sentence runs on beyond this unit; sanies is putrid matter or gore.
notes.44687.3: 44687 ends a list of names ([Satur]ninus, Domitia Attiola); 'et si qui afuere', 'and if any were absent', is obscure here. In 44691 the '#' separates the edition's three forms of Dianae. capitularem (a head-covering?) and fascia (a band or wrapping) are uncertain; 'minus parte tertia' apparently means the gift is made less a third. Single restored letters inside otherwise legible words are not bracketed.
notes.51573.5: 51573.5 opens mid-word: 'rit' completes fecerit, '(who) has committed (the theft)', from the line before. 'corulo pare(n)tatur' is obscure: corulus is hazel, parentare is to make offerings to the dead. 51574: paganus may mean civilian or villager; dimitte is taken as 'forgive'. 52039: DAVIIS is left as printed (letters not resolved); Senilis and Senni[...] are names. Single restored letters inside otherwise legible words are not bracketed.
notes.79513.1.1: Side 1 has only the letter B; 79513.2.1 is isolated letters, left as printed. The verb ending '-revavit' (2.5) has lost its beginning; it must mean something like 'stole'. 'Ter[en]ti' is taken as 'son of Terentius' (it could be 'slave of'). The {a} in conq[u]{a}er[or] is a letter the editors delete. Single restored letters inside otherwise legible words are not bracketed.
